title: Item
description: One item: its file in items/ and the item that --json prints (DESIGN.md §2.1, §4.3). A field a later slice adds joins this schema in that slice.

id.description: The project key, a dash and a number from 1, such as BM-12. Never reused.

title.description: One line, with no control characters, line breaks or marks that reorder text (DESIGN.md §2.1).

labels.description: Free text, lowercased and de-duplicated (DESIGN.md §2.1). Left out while there are none.

items.description: One line, trimmed, with no capital letters.

design.description: A reference into a design doc, such as DESIGN.md#2.4, on one line. Left out when there isn't one.

written.description: The text of each criterion as it was written at create, each on one line (DESIGN.md §2.1). Only a criterion command from an interactive terminal changes it afterwards, so slice 11's T5 can tell, and say, when a criterion was reworded or dropped. In no particular order, and left out while there are none.

criteria.description: The Done when list (DESIGN.md §2.3), numbered from 1 in commands. Left out while there are none.

started.description: What the item's last start recorded (DESIGN.md §2.4, §4.3). Each start replaces it. Left out until the item is first started by slice 7 or later.

verification.description: How the item reached done (DESIGN.md §2.7). Present only while the item is done: reopening moves it to previous_verification. Files written by slice 2 can still hold one on a shelved item.

previous_verification.description: The item's last verification record, from before it was last reopened. Each reopen from done replaces it. Left out until the item is first reopened from done.

holds.description: The triggers that fired at the item's last submit, each with the message saying why, while it waits in review for a human to approve or reject it (DESIGN.md §2.5). Present only while the item is in review, and left out otherwise.

history.description: One entry per move between states or edit, oldest first. Left out while there are none.

description.description: Free markdown. Left out when there isn't one.

key.description: A project key: up to 10 capital letters and digits, starting with a letter, such as BM.

sha.description: A git commit's full SHA: 40 hex digits, or 64 in a SHA-256 repository.

time.description: An RFC 3339 time in UTC, to the second.

hold.description: One trigger that fired (DESIGN.md §2.5): its name, such as T6, the message saying why it holds the item, and the files that fired it, if it is about files.

files.description: For a trigger about changed files, such as T4, the files that fired it, each relative to the project's root. show --diff lists them before the diff. Left out for a trigger that isn't about files, and in holds written before TR-6.

criterion.description: One criterion (DESIGN.md §2.3): what must be true, and how it's verified. With check, a script criterion. With ask, a judge criterion, whose inputs, each, context_lines and keep_comments say what its questions are asked about (DESIGN.md §2.3.1). With neither, a manual one, which alone takes evidence.

text.description: What must be true, on one line.

check.description: A shell command, run in the project's root, whose exit code 0 shows the criterion holds. On one line.

inputs.description: For a judge: the files it reads, relative to the project's root, or diff for the item's changes.

each.description: For a judge: a regex. The questions are asked once per line it matches, about the lines around it. Without it, the whole input is the excerpt.

context_lines.description: For a judge with each: the lines shown either side of a match. The config's judge.context_lines when it's left out.

keep_comments.description: For a judge about comments: its excerpts keep them. Left out when false, and comments are stripped.

ask.description: For a judge: its yes/no questions, each asked in a call of its own.

evidence.description: For a manual criterion, a note saying where to look (gate G2). On one line.

judged.description: One judge question G3 asked, as gates, submit and a refusal list it (DESIGN.md §3): its ref, its criterion, the answer and reason, and what the answer means. pass is the answer that passes, fail refuses the gate, and unsure holds the item under T10.

question.description: One of a judge's yes/no questions (DESIGN.md §2.3.1).

id.description: Names the question in its ref, such as c2:src/import.js:57:suggests_next_step.

yes.description: What a yes means, on one line.

no.description: What a no means, on one line.

pass_when.description: The answer that passes. yes when it's left out, and no for a question about a defect.

by.description: auto: the gates passed and no trigger fired. human: approved from the inbox. unchecked: done before the gates proved the work against a commit, so no commit ties the checks to the work.

commit.description: The commit the checks ran against, as a full SHA: HEAD when G5 looked. Left out of unchecked records.

ref.description: The git ref that keeps commit, in the project's repository, so a rebase or gc can't lose it (DESIGN.md §2.7). Deleting the item removes it.

checks.description: Every check the submit ran, criterion checks first, then the project's, in order. Left out when none ran.

criterion.description: The criterion whose check it is, numbered from 1. Left out for a project check.

output.description: Its last 20 lines of output, stdout and stderr together, without a final line break. Each kept line is cut at 500 characters, the last of them `…`, if it's longer. Left out if it printed nothing.

judges.description: Every judge question the submit asked, one entry per question and excerpt, in order (DESIGN.md §4.3). Left out when the item has no judge.

ref.description: The question's ref (DESIGN.md §2.3.2): the criterion, the file:line of an each match, if it has one, and the question's id, such as c2:src/import.js:57:suggests_next_step.

request.description: The fingerprint of the request it was asked in, which names its answer in judge/cache/: a SHA-256 in 64 lower-case hex characters.

triggers.description: For a human record, the triggers that held the item in review, which approve accepted (DESIGN.md §2.7). Left out when none fired, as for an auto record.

note.description: Why the record says what it does, such as that no gates ran.

criteria_hash.description: A SHA-256 fingerprint, in lower-case hex, of the criteria (each without its evidence), the kind and the design at start (T5). Left out by trackers before slice 11.

head.description: The commit HEAD pointed to at start, as a full SHA (T14). Left out for a repository with no commits yet, and by trackers before slice 8.

checks.description: Each criterion check, run once at start, where failing is expected because the work isn't done yet (T13). Left out when the item had no criterion checks.

move.description: One move between states (DESIGN.md §2.2, §4.3), or one edit or criterion accept, which has from equal to to and names the fields it changed (DESIGN.md §2.1).

via.description: The command that made the move. `status <id> <state>` records the command it maps onto. unknown appears only in --json output, never in a file: it stands for a command this version doesn't know, read from a file a newer tracker wrote. Such a file is listed, but this version never writes it back.

interactive.description: Whether stdin was a terminal: true for my own moves, false for an agent's (DESIGN.md §2.6).

reason.description: Why. Present for shelve, reopen and reject, which need one, and left out otherwise. One line of at most 500 characters.

fields.description: For an edit, the fields it changed, in the item file's order, and for a criterion accept, written. Left out for a move.

kind_before.description: For an edit that changed kind, the kind it replaced, so the digest can list a move away from capability (DESIGN.md §2.6). Left out otherwise.

labels_removed.description: For an edit, the labels it removed, so the digest can list one that removed needs-review (DESIGN.md §2.6). Left out when it removed none.
